findings.title: An empty `where` passes as present
quotes: an implementation-gate finding with no `gap` or `where`
findings.fix: treat an empty value as missing, for example `not any(v for v in f.get(k, []))`, and add a test with `- where:` empty.

sources.situation: a juror writes `- where:` with nothing after it, or only the guidance comment. `blocks` stores `[""]`, so `missing = [k ... if not f.get(k)]` treats `where` as present. `gap` is then checked against GAPS, but `where` is never checked for content. The finding is accepted with `where: ""`, so the human gets a finding that points nowhere. The test `test_malformed_output_stays_invalid` only drops the whole line.

findings.reason: Line 117 does accept `- where:` with an empty value, because `blocks` stores `[""]`, which is a truthy list. The user's note says an empty `where` was accepted before this epic too. AC-14 and FR-11 say "reject as before" and name only a missing `gap` or `where`. This epic's change (case folding of labels) did not cause it. I could not run `git show 19c8e09` here, so the pre-epic behaviour is taken from the caller's note.

findings.title: `none` followed by any number of `.` or `!` is accepted
findings.fix: use `re.fullmatch(r"none[.!]?", text, re.I)` instead of `rstrip`, and add a `none..` case to the malformed-output test.

sources.situation: `.rstrip(".!")` removes every trailing `.` and `!`. `None...`, `none.!.!` and `none!!!` therefore read as no findings, although the AC allows one mark. `None.!` is also accepted, and the tests cover only the four listed spellings. The harm is small, but it widens what the parser accepts beyond the spec.

findings.note: Delegated by the human: `none!!` or `none...` alone still means no findings, so the looser match loses nothing; noted in the PR

findings.title: Labels that differ only in case merge, and the first one silently wins
quotes: reads those fields as if written in the expected form
findings.fix: reject a repeated single-valued field (all fields except `quote` and `run`) as an error, or add a test that fixes the intended behaviour.

sources.situation: a finding has `- gap: partial` and later `- Gap: contradicts`, or `- severity: minor` and `- Severity: blocker`. `blocks` lower-cases both into one list and the parser uses `[0]`, so the later value is dropped with no error. Before this change the capitalised line was ignored; now it is merged and then discarded. A juror who corrects a field by adding a second line sees no sign that the correction was ignored. Only `run` is joined, so the other fields behave this way.

findings.title: Trailing-mark rule is looser than AC-12
findings.fix: match the whole line with `re.fullmatch(r"none[.!]?", text, re.I)` and add a case like `none!!` to `test_malformed_output_stays_invalid`.

sources.situation: AC-12 and CT-6 allow `none` optionally followed by one `.` or `!`. `rstrip` removes every trailing `.` or `!`, so `none!!`, `none...` and `none.!` also parse as no findings. The test lists only the four allowed forms, so it can't catch this.

findings.note: Delegated by the human: `none!!` or `none...` alone still means no findings, so the looser match loses nothing; noted in the PR

findings.title: Prose before findings is not rejected
quotes: `None, but see F1` or `none yet` under `## Findings`
findings.fix: when the text before the first `### ` is not exactly a none line, and findings follow, add the error. Add a unit test with `None, but see F1` and `none yet` followed by a finding.

sources.situation: a juror writes `## Findings`, then the line `None, but see F1`, then `### F1 ...` with all fields. The first line of the section does not match `none\W*$`, so no error is added. `findings` holds F1, the output is valid, and the lens is accepted. AC-14 names this exact slip as malformed and says the parser "still rejects it as INVALID". The added test (`test_malformed_output_stays_invalid`) only covers `None, but see F1` and `none yet` with no findings, so this case is untested.

findings.reason: `None, but see F1` or `none yet` with no `###` finding is rejected, because line 144 fires when `findings` is empty. When valid `### F1` blocks follow, the findings are all present and parsed. Line 142 rejects the `None.` plus finding case that AC-14 lists as a contradiction. Prose ahead of valid findings loses nothing, and the spec does not say it must be rejected.

findings.title: Several trailing marks are accepted as no findings
quotes: `none` in any case optionally followed by one `.` or `!`
findings.fix: use one rule for both checks, such as `^none[.!]?$` on the whole section text, and add `NONE!!` to the none-slip test as an invalid case.

sources.situation: `## Findings` holds only `NONE!!` (or `None.!`). The no-findings check does `rstrip(".!")`, which strips every trailing mark, so the output is accepted as no findings. The same text with a finding after it is rejected by `none\W*$`. FR-9 allows one `.` or `!`, so the first case should be invalid, and the two checks disagree.

findings.note: Delegated by the human: `none!!` or `none...` alone still means no findings, so the looser match loses nothing; noted in the PR

findings.title: Trailing punctuation is stripped without a limit, so `none!!` and `none.!.` read as no findings
quotes: `none` in any case optionally followed by one `.` or `!`
findings.fix: match the whole text with `re.fullmatch(r"none[.!]?", text, re.I)`, and add a `none..` case to the malformed-output test.

sources.situation: a `## Findings` text of `none...` or `NONE!!` or `none.!` is accepted as no findings. `rstrip(".!")` removes any run of those characters, but the spec allows a single one. Nothing in `test_none_slips_mean_no_findings` or `test_malformed_output_stays_invalid` tries a doubled mark, so the over-acceptance is untested.
